failure_summary.description: Rejected claims by misreading structural feasibility or the exact scope of hypotheses and uniformity.
Chose unsupported extensions or added structural claims instead of the strongest conclusion established by the setup.

patch.reasoning: Several failures turned plausible recollections into unproved exceptions, generalizations, orbit classifications, or uniform-in-time conclusions. Make the proof burden for each added clause explicit and distinguish finite-horizon estimates from bounds uniform over all time. The subgroup-rank error is already directly covered by the current skill, so it needs no duplicate rule.

edits.content:
## Verify every added scope or structure claim
- When an option adds a broader class of inputs, a stronger conclusion, or a classification property to a valid base claim, isolate and establish that added clause separately. A result for the stated coloring class does not automatically extend to all finite colorings; invariance or matching dimension counts alone does not establish that every fiber is a single orbit, especially at special values.
- Treat a proposed exception or failure claim as requiring evidence too. Do not reject a theorem by recalling a vaguely related counterexample: verify that it satisfies the exact hypotheses, or derive the failure from an applicable result.

For estimates involving time, distinguish a bound on each fixed interval \([0,T]\) with a constant \(C_T\) from a bound valid for all \(t\ge 0\) with one constant independent of the time horizon. Do not promote fixed-time or finite-horizon control to global-in-time uniformity without support.
